messages:
alice: Quick check — running into a weird dim mismatch when using the Python SDK embedding stream + local batch helper. py client returns 1536-d vectors but our JS re-ranker expects 1024. Anyone seen auth/retry cause model fallback to a smaller model?

ben: Hmm, auth fallback is a good call. If token scopes are limited we sometimes fall back to a 'safemode' model. What model name are you calling?

alice: Using model="openlm-mid-embed" (from our model-catalog). Code is just:

```python
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'])
embs = []
for batch in my_batcher(stream=True):
    resp = c.embeddings.create(model="openlm-mid-embed", input=batch)
    embs.extend(resp.data)
```

Outputs show shape 1536.

carla: Are you streaming partial responses? JS SDK sometimes post-processes dims when streaming + retries merge messages incorrectly.

dmitri: Also check quantization/float32 vs float16; but that shouldn't change length.

ben: Another quick check: print c.config.endpoint and c.auth.scopes to ensure same endpoint as prod. If you hit a deprecated region we route to a compatibility model.

alice: endpoint is https://api.redwood.example/v1, scopes seem full. I grep logs and saw a 502 retry then a 200 from a different host around the same call.

ci-bot: deploybot: noticed transient 502s in eu-central-1 between 09:12–09:15 UTC, autoscaler rotated a host.

carla: That rotation could explain it — fallback host may not have model vendor binaries, so we return a smaller shim model. Ops should have rollout notes.

sdk-ops: quick ping — can you paste a minimal repro that triggers the 1536 vectors? Also include headers from the failing request (redact keys).

alice: repro in Python above. headers during 502:

```
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
User-Agent: redwood-py/0.9.3
X-Request-Id: r-abc123
```

and the successful follow-up returned from host h-027 had body with model: "openlm-mini-embed".

dmitri: bingo — mini vs mid. The retry landed on a host serving "openlm-mini-embed" which is 1536? Wait that'd be larger. Could be catalog rename.

ben: Catalog mapping changed during that deploy window — mini was temporarily remapped to a different paramization (ugh). Two action items: 1) add a client-side check that verifies embedding dim matches expected per model (raise or log). 2) server: ensure retries preserve model variant affinity or include model-id in retry routing.

alice: I can PR client check. Proposed heuristic: after first batch, assert len(vector)==EXPECTED_DIM[model] and if mismatch, raise EmbeddingDimMismatchError with request id.

carla: Yep, that would catch it earlier. Keep it opt-out (env REDWOOD_STRICT_DIM=true) so we don't break existing customers.

sdk-ops: We'll also add a server header X-Model-Served: openlm-mini-embed to help debug routing in future.

alice: Thanks — I'll open the PR and link the failing request ids. Also adding a test that simulates a host changing model on retry.

ben: ty! if you need help with the JS side I can add a similar dim guard in the re-ranker.

alice: Great — will do. :thumbsup:
